function: Handover and user association: a multi-agent hysteretic deep recurrent Q-network decides the handover of each RIS subarray (p. 20, p. 22); the generative imputation-forecasting only predicts user-tracking and blockage sensing information for it (p. 13).
notes: The PDF is arXiv:2305.00135v1 (p. 1); its title and authors match the DOI (IEEE TWC 23(9), 2024). Reason above_phy: the learned decision is handover and user association. p. 20: "we thus, formulate the handover and user association problem of an RIS-assisted THz indoor network serving XR users"; p. 22: "The action of each agent is to perform a handover decision or to maintain the currently active link." The other learned part (non-autoregressive generative imputation and adversarial sparse transformer, p. 15-17) predicts the missing and future sensing vectors [AoA, AoD, ToA] (p. 13) that trigger handovers (eq. 13, p. 19) and feed the agents' observations (p. 22). It is not channel prediction (area 2): p. 13: "Instead, they provide RIS-operated BSs instantaneous and continual information about the users’ behavior and their corresponding varying environments", and it is scored by prediction accuracy (Fig. 6, p. 25). No beam, precoder, RIS phase, power, or waveform is learned, so neither area 3 nor area 5 applies: the sensing parameters come from CP tensor decomposition solved by alternating least squares (p. 11, p. 28), initial beam alignment uses existing techniques (p. 7), and the beam is re-pointed from the tracked angles (p. 22). Alternative code for the reviewer: if the AoA/AoD/ToA forecasting is taken as physical-layer learning that passes check 4, the work fails check 5 instead (function: user tracking and blockage prediction, akin to positioning), so the decision is exclude either way.
